title: Cross-household isolation E2E test (epic gate)
goal: The test that proves S-60's RLS policies actually fire once the app connects the right way -- not just that they're declared. This is the hard merge gate for E-21 per ADR-0006 and the ship-epic security gate; it does not get treated as optional or deferred.
in_scope: New e2e/isolation.spec.ts. Test setup: create two households (A, B) via the real signup flow (S-57), each with one distinct seeded item (via manual entry or direct DB insert against each household's own id).

Log in as household A's user. For every gated route (inventory, review, plan, shopping-list, insights, settings), assert only household A's data is visible -- household B's item never appears in any list.

Directly probe a household-B-scoped resource by id (item detail URL, receipt id, etc.) while logged in as household A -- assert it's denied (404/403), not silently returned. This is the part a list-filtering bug alone wouldn't catch: RLS must deny it at the query level, not just at the UI's rendering layer.
Repeat login as household B's user and assert the mirror image (B sees only B's data, A's resources are denied).
out_of_scope: Performance/load testing of RLS -- correctness only, not scale.
acceptance: e2e/isolation.spec.ts passes: household A's authenticated session cannot read, list, or write household B's row via any route, verified both by list-view absence and by direct-id-probe denial; same in reverse. This test is required green before ship-epic merges E-21 -- treat a failure here as blocking, not a follow-up.
invariants: This test must exercise the real request-scoped client path (a live authenticated session), not a service-role bypass -- testing against service-role would prove nothing about RLS.
Do not weaken this test to only check list-view filtering -- the direct-id-probe assertion is the one that actually distinguishes 'RLS enforces this' from 'the UI happens to filter it.'
